notes: doi:10.1074/jbc.M110.211078 -> PMID 21385872 / PMC3089498 (Sikora et al., JBC 2011), V. cholerae El Tor N16961 T2-secretome proteomics. Organism+strain (N16961 El Tor) exact match. Quote 'three hypothetical proteins encoded by VCA0583, VCA0738, and VC2298' is verbatim in abstract; these are listed among T2S substrates from an unbiased secretome analysis. Documents T2S-dependent secretion (secretome MS + confirmed T2S-dependent transport).

Same ref as T2SS_01 (PMID 21385872/PMC3089498). Quote '16 new putative T2S substrates, including sialidase, several proteins participating in chitin utilization, two aminopeptidases, TagA-related protein, cytolysin' is a verbatim prefix of the abstract sentence (continues '...RbmC, three hypothetical proteins...'). TagA-related protein (Q9KN18) listed among 16 new T2S substrates. Organism V. cholerae N16961 exact match.

doi:10.3389/fmicb.2011.00155 -> PMID 21811488 / PMC3140646 (Bleves et al., Front Microbiol 2011), a P. aeruginosa secretion-systems REVIEW. Quote 'there is only one Hxc-dependent substrate, namely LapA, known as low-molecular weight alkaline phosphatase (Ball et al.,)' verbatim in full text. Documents Hxc-T2SS-dependent secretion of LapA (machinery-dependent export). Organism P. aeruginosa PAO1 match. Confidence medium: source is a review citing primary (Ball et al.) rather than the primary experimental paper, but it does state machinery-dependent secretion.

Same ref as T2SS_03 (PMID 21811488/PMC3140646 review). Quote 'achieves the secretion of all Xcp substrates but the aminopeptidase PaAP (Michel et al.,). This is another indication of a specific interaction between the XcpP/XcpQ-like subcomplex and T2SS substrates.' verbatim in full text. PaAP is an Xcp(T2SS) substrate; documents machinery-dependent secretion. Organism PAO1 match. Confidence medium: review citing primary (Michel et al.).

doi:10.1128/IAI.70.11.6094-6106.2002 -> PMID 12379686 / PMC130422 (Flieger et al., Infect Immun 2002), L. pneumophila plaA lysophospholipase A. Quote 'We previously showed that Legionella pneumophila secretes, via its type II secretion system, phospholipase A activities ... we identified and characterized plaA, a gene encoding a phospholipase A that cleaves fatty acids from lysophospholipids.' matches abstract verbatim except PMC strips italic species/gene names (Legionella pneumophila, plaA) which appear in original; '...' bridges intervening clause. Documents T2SS secretion + culture-supernatant lipolytic assay (plaA mutant supernatants lost >80% activity). Organism L. pneumophila (Philadelphia-1 lineage) match.

doi:10.1074/jbc.272.17.11109 -> PMID 9111006 (Letellier, Howard, Buckley, JBC 1997). Quote 'Aeromonas spp. secrete the channel-forming protein proaerolysin across their inner and outer membranes in separate steps using the general secretion pathway.' is the verbatim first sentence of the abstract. Documents general secretion pathway (T2SS) export of proaerolysin across the outer membrane (energetics study of secretion). Organism: row A. hydrophila ATCC 7966; paper studies A. hydrophila (and A. salmonicida); species match, strain not specified in paper. DOI resolved via PubMed metadata.

doi:10.1128/IAI.00672-15 -> PMID 26169274 / PMC4567643 (DuMont et al., Infect Immun 2015), S. maltophilia K279a. Quote 'the serine proteases StmPr1 and StmPr2, which were confirmed to be Xps substrates, are predominantly responsible for secreted proteolytic activities exhibited by strain K279a' verbatim in abstract. Xps = T2SS; StmPr1 confirmed Xps(T2SS) substrate; documents secreted proteolytic activity. Organism + strain K279a exact match.

doi:10.1128/jb.179.23.7321-7330.1997 -> PMID 9393696 / PMC179682 (Shevchik et al., J Bacteriol 1997), pectate lyase PelI. Quote 'PelI is an extracellular protein secreted by the Out secretory pathway of E. chrysanthemi.' verbatim in abstract. Out = T2SS; documents T2SS-dependent extracellular secretion. Organism: row Dickeya dadantii 3937 = former name Erwinia chrysanthemi 3937 (same strain, genus renamed); flagged as synonym not strain_diff (identical organism). Match yes.
